title: Register configuration satisfies the middle invariant
statement: Let $m,d$ be nonnegative integers, let $\Lambda$ be a state set, and fix a Boolean input $x$, an register machine $A$ with $m$ registers and $d$ deciders, an initial label $l_0$, a label $l$, register values $v$, an output word $out$, a register $r$, a phase-augmented state $s$, a tape content function $f:\mathbb Z\to\mathrm{Option}(\{0,1\})$, and integers $q,W$. If the program associated to $A$ has no decider call at state $s$, $-1\le q\le W$, and $0\le W$, then the configuration obtained from the initial register configuration by setting its state to $s$, replacing register $r$'s tape by $f$ with head at $q$, satisfies the middle invariant: it has no decider call at its current state, and every register head lies between $-1$ and $W$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: A is a register machine with m registers and d deciders
v assigns natural-number values to the registers
s is a state-label and phase pair
f assigns an optional Boolean symbol to each integer tape cell
the program has no decider call at s
